intro: A summary may preserve a reference sequence while inserting unrelated words. ROUGE-L separates longest-subsequence recall from precision to reveal that tradeoff.
task: Measure retained sequence structure and explain why adding unrelated candidate words changes precision but not recall.
requirements: candidate and reference are token lists or tuples with nonempty strings and at most 500 tokens each.
Find the longest common subsequence length L, preserving order but allowing gaps. Return dict lcs, precision=L/len(candidate), recall=L/len(reference), f1=2PR/(P+R).
A zero denominator gives 0 for that component, including both-empty input. This is single-reference token ROUGE-L F1, without stemming or sentence aggregation.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Subsequence is not substring
hints.body: Matching tokens can be separated by gaps; preserve their relative order.

hints.title: Check both denominators
hints.body: Precision divides by candidate length and recall by reference length.

explanation: The longest common subsequence rewards preserved order without demanding contiguous matches. Inserting irrelevant candidate text leaves recall unchanged but lowers precision.
This deliberately explicit single-reference variant omits tokenization, stemming, and sentence-level aggregation. Metric names alone do not specify those evaluation choices.
